# Part 1

## Objective
Using 2023 data from the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s former Environmental Justice Screening and Mapping Tool (EJScreen) as well as data from the Mapping Inequality project at the University of Richmond's Digital Scholarship Lab, this section explores historical redlining in Los Angeles and its legacy on present-day environmental justice.

## Load packages

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(gt)
```

## Import data 

```{r}
# Read in geodatabase of EJScreen data at the Census Block Group level
ejscreen <- sf::st_read("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-hw2/data/ejscreen/EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb") 

# Filter to LA County
los_angeles <- ejscreen |> 
  dplyr::filter(ST_ABBREV == "CA") |> 
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME %in% c("Los Angeles County"))

# Read in json file
redline <- sf::st_read("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-hw2/data/mapping-inequality/mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json")

# Check that the CRS matches for ejscreen and redline
if(st_crs(redline) == st_crs(ejscreen)) {
  print("CRS matches") 
} else {
  warning('CRS does not match')
  print(paste('redline CRS is', st_crs(redline)))
  print(paste('ejscreen CRS is', st_crs(ejscreen)))
}

# Update redline crs to match ejscreen and run the test again 
redline <-st_transform(redline, 3857)

# Check that the CRS matches for ejscreen and redline
if(st_crs(redline) == st_crs(ejscreen)) {
  print("CRS matches") 
} else {
  warning('CRS does not match')
  print(paste('redline CRS is', st_crs(redline)))
  print(paste('ejscreen CRS is', st_crs(ejscreen)))
}
```


## Visualize data

```{r}
  # Create a map of historical redlining neighborhoods, including neighborhoods colored by HOLC grade, an appropriate base map, a clear title and legend 

tm_shape(redline) +
  tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
  tm_polygons() + 
  tm_fill(
    fill = "grade",
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "HOLC grade", position = tm_pos_out("right"))
  ) +
  tm_title(text = "Historical Redlining Neighborhoods in Los Angeles, CA") +
  tm_compass() +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_credits("Map 1", position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom"));
```

```{r}
# Join LA and redline spatial data to create a summary
la_redline <- st_join(los_angeles, redline, join = st_intersects)

# Create the summary data frame 
la_block_groups <- la_redline |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  mutate(Grade = grade) |> 
  group_by(Grade) |> 
  summarize(`Block Count` = n()) |> 
  mutate(Grade = replace_na(Grade, "Missing")) |> 
  mutate(`% of Census Blocks` = (`Block Count` / sum(`Block Count`)) * 100)

# Convert the data frame to a table using gt()
la_block_groups |> 
  gt()
```

```{r}
# Summarize average conditions by grade
avg_low_inc <- la_redline |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  drop_na(grade) |> 
  summarise(avg_pct_low_inc = mean(LOWINCPCT, na.rm = TRUE))

avg_pm25 <- la_redline |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  drop_na(grade) |> 
  summarise(avg_pct_pm25 = mean(P_PM25, na.rm = TRUE))

avg_life_exp <-  la_redline |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  drop_na(grade) |> 
  summarise(avg_pct_life_exp = mean(LIFEEXPPCT, na.rm = TRUE))

# Visualize average conditions by grade
ggplot(
  data = avg_low_inc,
  mapping = aes(
    x = grade,
    y = avg_pct_low_inc, 
    fill = grade
  )
) + 
geom_col() + 
theme_bw() +
labs(x = "HOLC grade", y = "Mean percent low income", title = "Percent low income by HOLC grade", caption = "Figure 1")

ggplot(
  data = avg_pm25,
  mapping = aes(
    x = grade,
    y = avg_pct_pm25, 
    fill = grade
  )
) + 
geom_col() + 
theme_bw() +
labs(x = "HOLC grade", y = "Mean percent PM 2.5", title = "Percent PM 2.5 by HOLC grade", caption = "Figure 2")

ggplot(
  data = avg_life_exp,
  mapping = aes(
    x = grade,
    y = avg_pct_life_exp, 
    fill = grade
  )
) + 
geom_col() + 
theme_bw() +
labs(x = "HOLC grade", y = "Mean percent low life expectancy", title = "Percent low life expectancy by HOLC grade", caption = "Figure 3")
```

## Interpretation

Map 1 utilizes the Los Angeles redlining spatial data to visualize the historical redlining neighborhoods across Los Angeles, California. Figures 1-3 utilize 2023 EJScreen data (specifically average percent low income, average percent PM 2.5 pollution, and average percent low life expectancy) combined with Los Angeles redlining data to look at how these conditions vary by Home Owners’ Loan Corporation (HOLC) grade in LA. Across all three figures, the proportion of negative attributes increases from grade A to grade D - meaning that grade D has the highest average percent of low income, the highest average percent of PM 2.5 pollution, and the highest average percent of low life expectancy, while grade A has the lowest proportion of these negative conditions. This is consistent with the finding that historical redlining practices have negative and lasting consequences on community wealth and community health.

# Part 2

## Objective
Utilizing data from the Mapping Inequality project at the University of Richmond's Digital Scholarship Lab as well as data from the Statewide Integrated Traffic Records System (SWITRS) database, this section explores the legacy of historical redlining in Los Angeles on the occurrence of pedestrian and bike crashes/fatalities from 2020 to 2025. 

## Import data

```{r}
# Read in crashes data, and inspect lat/long columns
crash_test <- read_csv("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-hw2/data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv")
sum(is.na(crash_test$POINT_X))
sum(is.na(crash_test$POINT_Y))
sum(is.na(crash_test$LATITUDE))
sum(is.na(crash_test$LONGITUDE))

# Import the crashes data as sf
crashes <- read_csv("/Users/courtneylorey/Desktop/GitHub/eds223/eds223-hw2/data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv") |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  drop_na(POINT_X) |>
  drop_na(POINT_Y) |> 
  rename(long = POINT_X,
          lat = POINT_Y) |> # Use POINT_X and POINT_Y as lat/long (as it has far fewer NAs)
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |> 
  st_transform(crs = 3857) # Set crs to match that of redline (3857)
```

## Visualize data

```{r}
# Before joining, check that the datasets have matching CRS
if(st_crs(redline) == st_crs(crashes)) {
  print("CRS matches") 
} else {
  warning('CRS does not match')
  print(paste('redline CRS is', st_crs(redline)))
  print(paste('crashes CRS is', st_crs(crashes)))
}

# Join redline data with crash data
redline_crashes <- st_join(crashes, redline)

# Select relevant columns from crash data
filtered_redline_crash <- redline_crashes |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  mutate(
    grade = ifelse(is.na(grade), "HOLC Grade Missing", grade)
  ) |> 
  select(grade, long, lat, PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT, BICYCLE_ACCIDENT) |> 
  filter(PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y" | BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> 
  count(grade) |> 
  mutate(Percent = (n / sum(n)) * 100)

# Convert the data frame to a table using gt()
gt(filtered_redline_crash)

# Visualize 
ggplot(
  data = filtered_redline_crash,
  mapping = aes(
    x = grade,
    y = Percent, 
    fill = grade
  )
) + 
geom_col() + 
theme_bw() +
labs(x = "HOLC grade", y = "Percent accidents", title = "Percentage of pedestrian and bike crashes and fatalities by HOLC grade", fill = "Grade", caption = "Figure 4")
```

## Interpretation

Figure 4 shows that for pedestrian and bike accidents (including crashes and fatalities) that occurred in Los Angeles within a given HOLC-graded area between 2020 and 2025, the largest proportion of accidents occured within HOLC grades C (27%) and D (14%). HOLC grades C and D experienced significantly more accidents than HOLC grades A and B. This demonstrates an outsized occurence of accidents in areas with lower HOLC grades, indicating that these redlined neighborhoods are at a higher risk of accidents, and that highly graded areas are safer from accidents. This is consistent with the finding that historical redlining continues to have detrimental impacts on present-day community health.

It is also worth noting that the majority (52%) of accidents occurred in areas that did not have an assigned HOLC grade (grade was listed as NA in the data set).
